212.notes: SAFEGUARDING FLAG - HANDLE THIS ROW DIFFERENTLY FROM THE REST OF THE COHORT. Agatha Amani House is not an ecovillage in the usual sense: it is A SAFE SHELTER FOR SURVIVORS OF SEXUAL AND DOMESTIC VIOLENCE, a registered Kenyan charitable trust, and reportedly the first refuge of its kind in Kenya offering extended stays with psychosocial support and skills training. It appears in GEN because it runs regenerative agriculture and permaculture on site as part of its healing and sustainability programme. TWO CONSEQUENCES FOLLOW. First, methodological: this is a single institutional compound - a main house with an attached kitchen and training room and an on-site well, completed in 2014 - not a settlement, so settlement-scale metrics do not apply and it should probably be reported separately from the rest of the cohort. Second, and more important, ETHICAL: publishing precise coordinates, high-resolution imagery or anything that could identify residents of a domestic-violence refuge carries a real risk to the people sheltered there. Any output that names or locates this site should be reviewed on that basis before publication, whatever the rest of the protocol says. On-site activity: crops plus goats, cows, chickens and rabbits, both for consumption and for sale at the local market; a sanitary-pad machine; baking and sewing programmes.
